messages:
matt: Quick heads-up — I found a mismatch on the Embeddings API docs. The request example on /api/embeddings uses `input: "single string"` but the server expects `inputs: [string]` for batch semantics. Repro with current example returns 400 on latest hosted runtime.

carmen: oof. which doc file is that? link pls.

matt: It's the example block in docs/api/embeddings.md (line ~42 on the site). PR I started is here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3456 but haven't pushed the snippet updates yet.

sylvia: thanks for flagging. We also ship SDK snippets that mirror that example. I can update the Python/Go snippets in the PR if we standardize on one canonical example.

kevin: we should also check the OpenAPI example and the sample response shape. I vaguely remember the response example uses `embedding` singular instead of `embeddings` array. That'll confuse automated snippet generation.

matt: good call — I noticed that too. Current page shows response: `{ "embedding": [0.1, 0.2] }` which is wrong; correct shape is `{ "embeddings": [[...], [...]] }` for batch.

jordan: FYI CI for the docs site will fail if we change the example shape without updating the codegen tests (they assert example/responses match schemas). I'll attach CI run for the PR.

matt: here's my proposed minimal change: update request example to a batch array, show a one-line note about single-item shims, fix the response to be an array of embeddings, and update SDK snippets. Example to land in docs: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"open-embedding-1","inputs":["first text","second text"]}'
```

Python snippet:

```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=TOKEN)
res = client.embeddings.create(model='open-embedding-1', inputs=['first text','second text'])
# res.embeddings -> [[...], [...]]
```

carmen: I like a single canonical batch example + a tiny note: "If you pass a single string, wrap it in an array (inputs=[...]) — legacy single-string examples will continue to be accepted by older clients." keeps things clear without duplicating examples.

kevin: add to that note: mention that some older SDK versions accepted a string and coerced it; new versions require array. Put a migration line like: "If your client sent a string, update to wrap it in an array; see migration guide."

sylvia: I'll update the Go and Ruby snippets accordingly. Also will add a small unit test in sdk-snippets CI to validate request example serialization.

matt: I'll update the OpenAPI example object in the same PR so codegen stays happy. Plan:
- change docs/api/embeddings.md request+response examples to array shapes
- update openapi/spec.yaml example entries
- update python/go/ruby snippets in docs repo
- add a short migration note in docs/migration/embeddings.md
- run codegen and fix failing snippet-tests

jordan: ping me when PR is ready, I'll re-run codegen and CI. If tests need changes in the snippet validator, we'll coordinate in eng-platform channel.

matt: created branch docs/embeds-batch-example, pushed initial edits, updated the curl + python examples, left TODO for SDK snippets. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3456 (WIP).

deploy-bot: deploy preview available: https://deploy-preview-3456--docs.redwood.ai (expires in 7 days) :rocket: 

kevin: small nit — while editing, please update the sample response in the 'Examples' section that we use on marketing pages (they sometimes copy that snippet). We want consistency across product docs and marketing samples.

carmen: agreed. Also add a short test case to the docs test harness that tries both single-string and array inputs and asserts the examples in the page match the OpenAPI schemas. Helps prevent regressions.

sylvia: done — I pushed snippet updates to the PR (python/go/ruby). I left both a minimal single-item example in a "Compatibility" note and the canonical batch example as the main sample.

matt: merged after reviews. CI flagged one remaining issue: the OpenAPI generator expected `embeddings` field name in responses but our codegen used `data` historically. Jordan is fixing the codegen mapping, but to unblock docs we added a compatibility example showing both shapes.

jordan: created fix in codegen-tooling to align response field names. Open ticket: https://github.com/redwood-inference/codegen/issues/812. Will roll out a patch tomorrow and re-run docs generation.

kevin: thanks. Once codegen patch lands, please re-run the snippet tests and remove the temporary compatibility duplicate example. We should not ship two canonical examples long-term.

matt: final checklist I pushed to the PR description: change log entry, redirect from old example URL, add migration note, update marketing copy, and verify SDK snippet tests. Thanks team :thumbsup:
